a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is a small neutral pyrazolone (MW 188, logD 1.48, TPSA 26.9, no H-bond donors, one rotatable bond); the supplied physicochemical prior is high, but no direct query-specific bioavailability measurement is present.

The closest L5 pyrazolone analog edaravone (M04) showed very high intestinal permeability (Papp > 10 × 10^-6 cm/s in rat intestine/MDCKII) and no P-gp efflux in hMDR1-MDCKII cells (efflux ratio < 1, unchanged by verapamil), indicating no gut-wall efflux barrier for this pyrazolone class.

Other L5 records for small neutral/lipophilic molecules show high permeability and no appreciable efflux: tryptanthrin ER ~0.96–1.12, warfarin ER 0.9–1.0, aspirin ER < 1.5, and phenobarbital transport unaffected by P-gp inhibitors; these are mechanistically consistent with favorable intestinal absorption.

All visible L1 gold records in transferable contexts report measured oral bioavailability at or above 30%: urapidil 78%/72%/69%, alogliptin ~100%, alprazolam SR >84%, trazodone 63–91%, eltrombopag ≥52%, ziprasidone 30% fasted, ondansetron 40% with rifampin, pirfenidone high, and teneligliptin 75–87%.
